title: Basic Model Run
text: can get started simplest model run almost entirely default model parameters. parameter malariasimple requires define initial EIR (init_EIR)
code: library(malariasimple)  ##------------------- Define default parameters ---------------------- params <- get_parameters() |>   set_equilibrium(init_EIR = 10)  ##----------------------- Run model ---------------------------------- out <- run_simulation(params) |> as.data.frame()  ##-------------------- Plot PfPR[2-10] ------------------------------ plot(x = out$time, y = out$n_detect_730_3650/out$n_730_3650,      type = "l", lwd = 2,      xlab = "Days", ylab = expression(paste(italic(Pf),"PR"[2-10])),      ylim = c(0,1))

title: Basic Model Run
text: Simulating model malariasimple two-step process: first define parameters, run model. can define core parameters using helper function get_parameters(). detailed description parameters default values, refer documentation running ?get_parameters. key function preparing parameters set_equilbrium(). calculates equilibrium parameters specified initial EIR. function also provides ‘finishing touches’ parameter list order satisfy model. therefore essential set_equilbrium() called end parameter preparing process.
code: custom_params <- get_parameters(n_days = 200, #Length of simulation                                 human_population = 1000, #Size of human population                                 eta = 1/(30*365)) |> #Human population birth/death rate   set_equilibrium(init_EIR = 10) custom_out <- run_simulation(custom_params)

title: Basic Model Run
text: Malaria treatment therapies built core structure model inclusion Treated (T) Prophylactically Protected (P) states (see model_introduction vignette). given proportion cases successfully treated enter Treated state protected superinfection infectiousness mosquitoes approximately two-thirds lower untreated individuals. progress ‘Prophylactically Protected’ state fully protected infection contribute overall force infection. Treatment programmes can customised setting following parameters get_parameters() function: daily_ft: proportion cases promptly effectively treated. can given either scalar value (treatment coverage assumed constant throughout simulation), vector daily values. (Default = 0) rT: individuals leave Treated state rate rT, .e. time spent state assumed follow exponential distribution mean 1 / rT. (Default = 1/5 days-1) rP: individuals leave Prophylactically Protected state rate rP, .e. time spent state assumed follow exponential distribution mean 1 / rP. (Default = 1/15 days-1)
code: treatment_params <- get_parameters(n_days = 200,                                    daily_ft = 0.7, #Assume 70% of cases are effectively and promptly treated throughout the simulation                                    rT = 1/3, #Treated individuals remain infectious for an average of 3 days                                    rP = 1/20, #Treated individuals retain prophylactic protection for an additional 20 days                                    ) |>    set_equilibrium(init_EIR = 10) treatment_out <- run_simulation(treatment_params)

title: Basic Model Run
text: get_parameters(), can define age groups want model output regarding clinical incidence prevalence. essential align age compartments defined age_vector (default values, see ?get_parameters). ages must provided days. align malariasimulation, prevalence inferred proportion detected infections (n_detect_) population proportion within age group (n_) following examples request prevalence clinical incidence two age groups: Ages 2-10 Everyone
code: ##--------------------- Define age categories ------------------------ age_vector <- c(0,1,2,5,10,20,40,60,100)*365 min_age_render <- c(2,0)*365 max_age_render <- c(10,Inf)*365  ## --------------------- Set up model parameters -------------------- params_ages <- get_parameters(n_days = 100,                               age_vector = age_vector,                               clin_inc_rendering_min_ages = min_age_render,                               clin_inc_rendering_max_ages = max_age_render,                               prevalence_rendering_min_ages = min_age_render,                               prevalence_rendering_max_ages = max_age_render) |>   set_equilibrium(init_EIR = 10)  ## -------------------------- Run model -------------------------- out_ages <- run_simulation(params_ages) |> as.data.frame()  ## Plot par(mfrow = c(1,2)) plot(x = out_ages$time, y = out_ages$n_clin_inc_0_Inf / out_ages$n_0_Inf,      type = "l", col = "#F8766D", ylim = c(0,0.0025),lwd = 2,      xlab = "Days", ylab = "Clinical incidence (cases per person per day)") lines(out_ages$time, out_ages$n_clin_inc_730_3650 / out_ages$n_730_3650,       col = "#00BFC4",lwd=2) legend("bottomright", legend = c("All ages", "Ages 2-10"),        col = c("#F8766D", "#00BFC4"), lty = 1,        bty = "n", ncol = 1, cex = 0.8, lwd=2)  plot(out_ages$time, out_ages$n_detect_0_Inf / out_ages$n_0_Inf,      type = "l", col = "#F8766D", ylim = c(0,0.4), lwd=2,      xlab = "Days", ylab = "Prevalence") lines(out_ages$time, out_ages$n_detect_730_3650 / out_ages$n_730_3650,       col = "#00BFC4",lwd=2) legend("bottomright", legend = c("All ages", "Ages 2-10"),        col = c("#F8766D", "#00BFC4"), lty = 1,        bty = "n", ncol = 1, cex = 0.8, lwd=2)

title: Basic Model Run
text: can also use age rendering function plot age distribution certain outputs. show example output average age distribution clinical incidence. , report incidence per capita (cases per person per day) dividing age group’s incidence count (n_clin_inc_*) population (n_*), values scale plots .
code: age_vector <- c(0:100) * 365 min_age_render <- c(0:99) * 365 max_age_render <- c(1:100) * 365  ## --------------------- Set up model parameters -------------------- params_ages <- get_parameters(   n_days = 100,   age_vector = age_vector,   clin_inc_rendering_min_ages = min_age_render,   clin_inc_rendering_max_ages = max_age_render,   prevalence_rendering_min_ages = min_age_render,   prevalence_rendering_max_ages = max_age_render ) |>   set_equilibrium(init_EIR = 10)  ## -------------------------- Run model -------------------------- out_ages <- run_simulation(params_ages) |>    as.data.frame()  ## -------------------------- Plot age distribution  -------------------------- clin_cols <- grep("n_clin_inc", colnames(out_ages), value = TRUE) pop_cols  <- sub("n_clin_inc_", "n_", clin_cols)  # Per-capita clinical incidence (cases per person per day), averaged over time age_means <- vapply(   seq_along(clin_cols),   function(i) mean(out_ages[[clin_cols[i]]] / out_ages[[pop_cols[i]]], na.rm = TRUE),   numeric(1) ) barplot(   age_means,   col = "lightblue",   main = "Average Clinical Incidence by Yearly Age Group",   xlab = "Age group (years)",   ylab = "Clinical incidence (cases per person per day)" )

title: Basic Model Run
text: Seasonality can included model using set_seasonality() function. main argument coefficients Fourier function (FF) describing relative carrying capacity vector population time.
code: ##------------------ Define seasonal parameters -------------------- #Fourier Coefficients g0 <- 0.28 g <- c(-0.3, -0.03, 0.17) h <- c(-0.35, 0.33, -0.08)  #Floor argument defines minimal value of relative carrying capacity seasonal_params <- get_parameters(n_days = 365) |>   set_seasonality(g0 = g0,                    g = g,                   h = h,                   floor = 0.002) |>   set_equilibrium(init_EIR = 10)  ##------------------- Run simulation and plot --------------------- seasonal_output <- run_simulation(seasonal_params) |> as.data.frame()  par(mfrow = c(1,1)) plot(seasonal_output$time, seasonal_output$mv, lwd = 2,      type = "l", xlab = "Days", "ylab" = "Mosquito Population")

title: Basic Model Run
text: Simulations can also run stochastic human transitions. achieve , can simply add stochastic = TRUE get_parameters() function call. can also run multiple simulations setting n_particles parameter run_simulation(). produce 3D array dimensions [timesteps, variables, particles]. can converted long dataframe using make_2d().
code: set.seed(1) ##------------------- Prepare parameters --------------------- n_particles <- 5 n_days <- 365 stoch_params <- get_parameters(n_days = n_days,                                   stochastic = TRUE,                                   human_population = 1000) |>   set_seasonality(g0 = g0,                   g = g,                   h = h,                   floor = 0.002) |>   set_equilibrium(init_EIR = 10)  ##---------------------- Run simulation ---------------------- stochastic_output <- run_simulation(stoch_params, n_particles = n_particles) |> make_2d()  ##------------------------ Plot ------------------------------ # Define plot range plot_range <- range(c(stochastic_output$time, seasonal_output$time)) y_range <- range(c(stochastic_output$n_detect_730_3650 / stochastic_output$n_730_3650,                    seasonal_output$n_detect_730_3650 / seasonal_output$n_730_3650), na.rm = TRUE)  plot(NA, xlim = plot_range, ylim = y_range, xlab = "Time", ylab = expression(italic(Pf)~PR[2-10]), bty = "l")  # Add stochastic output for (i in unique(stochastic_output$particle)) {   subset_data <- stochastic_output[stochastic_output$particle == i, ]   lines(subset_data$time, subset_data$n_detect_730_3650 / subset_data$n_730_3650, col = "#F8766D", lwd = 1, lty = 1) }  # Add deterministic output lines(seasonal_output$time, seasonal_output$n_detect_730_3650 / seasonal_output$n_730_3650, col = "#619CFF", lwd = 2, lty = 1)  legend("topleft",        legend = c("Stochastic", "Deterministic"),        col = c("#F8766D", "#619CFF"),        bty = "n",        lty = c(1, 1),        lwd = c(1, 2))

title: Insecticide Treated Nets
text: malariasimple, ITNs interrupt feeding cycle mosquitoes. Upon attempting feed human protected ITN, three things can occur: mosquito successfully feeds continues oviposit (probability = sns_{n}) mosquito dies (probability = dnd_{n}) mosquito survives feeding attempt, repelled net searches new host (probability = rnr_{n}) Hence, effectiveness ITN intervention depends many people currently using ITNs successful ITNs given time killing repelling mosquitoes. factors can parameterised using set_bednets() function.

title: Insecticide Treated Nets
text: Efficacy ITN distribution assumed wane time two mechanisms: ITN insecticide decay. Decay assumed exponential defined half-life days gamman ITN loss. model assumes ITNs retained retention days, net longer used. deterministic approximatation malariasimulation net retention varies individuals, kept average retention days. Three parameters required fully parametrise ITNs. dn0 Probability mosquito dying upon encounter brand new net rn Probability mosquito repelled upon encounter brand new net rnm Probability mosquito repelled upon encounter old net (fully decayed insecticide)

title: Insecticide Treated Nets
text: default. model assumes ITNs distributed discrete distribution events (days) specified proportion population (coverages). Within assumption, can also choose decide gets net successive round. distribution_type = "random". ITNs distributed randomly event, probability receiving net unrelated whether received net previously. equivalent correlation = 0 malariasimulation. distribution_type = "correlated". assume individuals ‘accessible’ public health institutions others. case, new nets first distributed previously received net given new individuals case expanded coverage. Note: Assuming ‘random’ distribution can force size ITN compartment large. can increase numerical error introduced synthetically reduce effectiveness ITNs account periods lower coverage, especially high EIRs. Using set_bednets() discrete distribution Visualising discrete parameters set_bednets() tracks usage average insecticide decay distribution event. ITN usage can visualised using intermediate function get_itn_usage_mat(). model one compartment intervention, model takes total usage time point running simulation. , plot input model assumptions.
code: n_days <- 2 * 365 ## ------------------  Define ITN parameters -------------------------- itn_days <- c(100, 200, 350) #Days on which ITN distribution events occur itn_cov <- c(0.1, 0.4, 0.5) #Proportion of the population who receive an ITN on each distribution event gamman <- 2.64 * 365 #Half-life of insecticide retention <- 5 * 365 #People keep their nets for 5 years   ## -------------  Set up malariasimple parameters ---------------------- #Random distribution discrete_params_rand <- malariasimple::get_parameters(n_days = n_days) |>   malariasimple::set_bednets(     days = itn_days,     coverages = itn_cov,     gamman = gamman,     retention = retention,     distribution_type = "random"   ) |>   malariasimple::set_equilibrium(init_EIR = 10)  #Correlated distribution discrete_params_corr <- malariasimple::get_parameters(n_days = n_days) |>   malariasimple::set_bednets(     days = itn_days,     coverages = itn_cov,     gamman = gamman,     retention = retention,     distribution_type = "correlated"   ) |>   malariasimple::set_equilibrium(init_EIR = 10)  ## ---------------------- Run simulation ------------------------------ discrete_rand_out <- malariasimple::run_simulation(discrete_params_rand) |> as.data.frame() discrete_corr_out <- malariasimple::run_simulation(discrete_params_corr) |> as.data.frame()  ## -----------------------  Plot  ------------------------------------- plot(discrete_rand_out$time, discrete_rand_out$n_detect_730_3650/discrete_rand_out$n_730_3650,      type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "steelblue",       main = "Discrete Distributions",      xlab = "Day", ylab =  expression(paste(italic(Pf),"PR"[2-10]))) lines(discrete_corr_out$time, discrete_corr_out$n_detect_730_3650 / discrete_corr_out$n_730_3650,       lwd = 2, col = "firebrick") abline(v = itn_days, lty = 2) legend("topright",         legend = c("Random", "Correlated"),         col = c("steelblue", "firebrick"),        lty = c(2,2), bty = "n") ## -------------  Return usage and decay matrices ---------------------- usage_mat_rand <- get_itn_usage_mat(itn_days, itn_cov, retention, n_days, distribution_type = "random") usage_mat_corr <- get_itn_usage_mat(itn_days, itn_cov, retention, n_days, distribution_type = "correlated")  ## -----------------------  Plot  -------------------------------- t <- 1:n_days colours <- c("#1B9E77", "#D95F02", "#7570B3") par(mfrow = c(1, 2), cex = 0.6)   #Usage plot (random) matplot(t, usage_mat_rand[, seq_along(itn_days)], type = "l", lty = 1, col = colours, ylim = c(0,1),         xlab = "Time", ylab = "ITN usage", main = "Random Discrete Distribution") lines(1:n_days, discrete_params_rand$itn_eff_cov_daily[2:(n_days+1)] * discrete_params_rand$max_itn_cov,       col = "black", lwd = 2, lty = 2) legend("topleft",        legend = c("Distribution event 1", "Distribution event 2", "Distribution event 3", "Total ITN usage"),        col = c(colours, "black"),        lty = c(1, 1, 1, 2),        lwd = c(1, 1, 1, 2),        bty = "n")   #Usage plot (correlated) matplot(t, usage_mat_corr[, seq_along(itn_days)], type = "l", lty = 1, col = colours, ylim = c(0,1),         xlab = "Time", ylab = "ITN usage", main = "Correlated Discrete Distribution") lines(1:n_days, discrete_params_corr$itn_eff_cov_daily[2:(n_days+1)] * discrete_params_corr$max_itn_cov,       col = "black", lwd = 2, lty = 2) legend("topleft",        legend = c("Distribution event 1", "Distribution event 2", "Distribution event 3", "Total ITN usage"),        col = c(colours, "black"),        lty = c(1, 1, 1, 2),        lwd = c(1, 1, 1, 2),        bty = "n")

title: Insecticide Treated Nets
text: model assumes ITNs continually distributed individuals replacing nets every retention days. Using set_bednets() continuous distribution  Visualising continuous parameters continuous assumption, insecticide decay considered constant (equal mean decay retention period). ITN coverage input directly daily time series daily_continuous_cov. overlay total ITN usage (daily_continuous_cov) mean ITN efficacy: daily probability host-seeking mosquito killed repelled (1 - s_itn_daily). combines coverage (constant) mean insecticide effect, sits usage curve.
code: ## ------------------  Define ITN parameters -------------------------- itn_coverage_data <- data.frame(day = c(1, 365, 2 * 365), cov = c(0.2, 0.3, 0.8)) daily_continuous_cov <- approx(itn_coverage_data$day, itn_coverage_data$cov, xout = 1:n_days)$y  ## -------------  Set up malariasimple parameters ---------------------- continuous_params <- malariasimple::get_parameters(n_days = 2 * 365,                                                   age_vector = c(0, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 40, 60, 80) * 365) |>   malariasimple::set_bednets(continuous_distribution = TRUE,                              daily_continuous_cov = daily_continuous_cov) |>   malariasimple::set_equilibrium(init_EIR = 5)  ## ---------------------- Run simulation ------------------------------ continuous_out <- malariasimple::run_simulation(continuous_params) |> as.data.frame()  ## -----------------------  Plot  ------------------------------------- plot(continuous_out$time, continuous_out$n_detect_730_3650/continuous_out$n_730_3650,      type = "l", lwd = 2, main = "Continuous Distribution",      xlab = "Day", ylab =  expression(paste(italic(Pf),"PR"[2-10]))) ## -----------------------  Plot -------------------------------------- par(cex = 0.8) plot(   1:n_days,   daily_continuous_cov,   type = "l",   xlab = "Time",   ylab = "",   ylim = c(0, 1),   lty = 2,   lwd = 2 ) lines(   1:n_days,   1 - continuous_params$s_itn_daily[2:(n_days + 1)],   col = "red",   lty = 2,   lwd = 2 ) legend(   "bottomright",   legend = c("Total ITN usage", "Mean ITN efficacy"),   col = c("black", "red"),   lty = c(2, 2),   lwd = c(2, 2),   bty = "n" )

title: Seasonal Malaria Chemoprevention
text: SMC can introduced using set_smc() function. Drugs defined four main parameters: drug_efficacy drug_rel_c shape_smc scale_smc Preset values available SP_AQ, AL, DHA_PQP (see ?set_drug_params details). Alternatively, custom drug parameters can input directly. parameters, SMC influences transmission dynamics three ways: Prophylaxis Effect. Individuals receive SMC assumed protection infection probability PSMCP_{SMC}. PSMCP_{SMC} wanes according Weibull distribution defined parameters shape_smc scale_smc. modelled effective reduction force infection within compartments receiving SMC. Infection Clearing Effect. Individuals currently infected receiving SMC cleared infection probability drug_efficacy. Clearance occurs smc_clearance_lag days date SMC administration (default = 5 days). Reduced Infectivity. smc_clearance_lag days following SMC administration, currently infected individuals assumed reduced infectivity drug_rel_c. assumptions behind SMC parameterisation malariasimple largely based Thompson,2022 - Supplementary Materials.

title: Seasonal Malaria Chemoprevention
text: malariasimulation, can adjust ‘correlation’ intervention determine whether previously received intervention makes individual /less/equally likely receive intervention future. functionality currently exist malariasimple, however can set two extremes: ‘Random’ distribution individual within defined age category equal chance receiving SMC distribution event regardless whether received dose previously. Equivalent correlation = 0. ‘Correlated’ distribution Assumes doses given children round. child receives SMC first distribution event, continue receive doses unless coverage decreases. Equivalent correlation = 1.

title: Seasonal Malaria Chemoprevention
text: fully define SMC intervention, can specify: SMC Drug: drug (alternatively can manually define drug parameters) Days SMC administration events occur: days Proportion age-eligible children covered: coverages Minimum age eligible SMC: min_age Maximum age eligible SMC: min_age Note: SMC age boundaries must align age categories defined get_parameters() Now can set malariasimple parameters different scenarios run models
code: library(malariasimple) n_years <- 4 n_days <- 4 * 365  ##--------------------- Define Seasonality ------------------------- g0 <- 0.28 g <- c(-0.3, -0.03, 0.17) h <- c(-0.35, 0.32, -0.07)  ##--------------------- Define SMC parameters ---------------------- # Get day-of-year of peak vector carrying capacity peak_cc <- get_peak_cc(g0, g, h)  # Schedule SMC administrations relative to peak carrying capacity  smc_offsets <- c(-60, -30, 0, 30)  #Hence, define SMC administration days smc_days <- rep(365 * seq(1, n_years - 1, by = 1), each = length(smc_offsets)) +   peak_cc +   rep(smc_offsets, (n_years - 1))  #Assume linearly increasing SMC coverage from 30% -> 60% of target age group smc_cov <- seq(0.3, 0.6, length.out = length(smc_days)) ## ------------ Seasonal transmission with no interventions --------------- basic_params <- malariasimple::get_parameters(n_days = n_days,                                               age_vector = c(0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 10, 20, 40, 60, 80) *                                                 365) |>   malariasimple::set_seasonality(g0 = g0, g = g, h = h) |>   malariasimple::set_equilibrium(init_EIR = 10) basic_out <- malariasimple::run_simulation(basic_params) |> as.data.frame()  ## ---------- Seasonal transmission with 'random' SMC distribution -------- smc_random_params <- basic_params |>   malariasimple::set_smc(     coverages = smc_cov,     days = smc_days,     min_age = 1 * 365,     max_age = 5 * 365,     distribution_type = "random",     drug = "AL"   ) |>   malariasimple::set_equilibrium(init_EIR = 10) smc_random_out <- malariasimple::run_simulation(smc_random_params) |> as.data.frame()  ## ---------- Seasonal transmission with 'correlated' SMC distribution -------- smc_corr_params <- basic_params |>   malariasimple::set_smc(     coverages = smc_cov,     days = smc_days,     min_age = 1 * 365,     max_age = 5 * 365,     distribution_type = "correlated",     drug = "AL"   ) |>   malariasimple::set_equilibrium(init_EIR = 10) smc_corr_out <- malariasimple::run_simulation(smc_corr_params) |> as.data.frame()  ## --------------------------- Plot PfPR[2-10] ----------------------------  plot(basic_out$time, basic_out$n_detect_730_3650/basic_out$n_730_3650,      type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "#F8766D", ylim = c(0.1,0.5),      xlab = "Day", ylab =  expression(paste(italic(Pf),"PR"[2-10]))) lines(smc_random_out$time, smc_random_out$n_detect_730_3650/smc_random_out$n_730_3650,       type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "#00BA38",       xlab = "Day", ylab =  expression(paste(italic(Pf),"PR"[2-10]))) lines(smc_corr_out$time, smc_corr_out$n_detect_730_3650/smc_corr_out$n_730_3650,       type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "#619CFF",       xlab = "Day", ylab =  expression(paste(italic(Pf),"PR"[2-10]))) abline(v = smc_days, lty = 2) legend("bottomleft", legend = c("No intervention", "SMC (random)", "SMC (correlated)"),         col = c("#F8766D","#00BA38","#619CFF"), lty = 1,         bty = "n", ncol = 1, cex = 0.8, lwd=2)

title: Comparison with malariasimulation
code: n_years <- 3 human_pop <- 5000 n_days <- n_years*365 init_EIR <- 50 num_sims <- 10 #Number of parallel stochastic simulations  ##Seasonality parameters g0 <- 0.28 g <- c(-0.3, -0.03, 0.17) h <- c(-0.35, 0.32, -0.07)  ##Define ITN parameters itn_days <- c(100,365,500,800) itn_cov <- c(0.1,0.4,0.5,0.1) gamman <- 2.64*365 retention <- 5*365  ##Define SMC parameters smc_offsets <- c(-60, -30, 0, 30) peak_cc <- get_peak_cc(g0, g, h) smc_days <- rep(365 * seq(1, n_years - 1, by = 1), each = length(smc_offsets)) +   peak_cc +   rep(smc_offsets, 2) smc_cov <- seq(0.3,0.6, length.out = length(smc_days)) smc_min_age <- 0.25*365 smc_max_age <- 5*365

title: Comparison with malariasimulation
code: ##Set up malariasimulation parameters n_dist <- length(itn_days) dn0 <- rep(0.41, n_dist) rn <- rep(0.56, n_dist) rnm <- rep(0.24, n_dist) gamman_vec <- rep(gamman, n_dist)  malsim_params <- malariasimulation::get_parameters(   overrides = list(     model_seasonality = TRUE,     g0 = g0,     g = g,     h = h,     clinical_incidence_rendering_min_ages = 0,     clinical_incidence_rendering_max_ages = 100 * 365,     prevalence_rendering_min_ages = 2 * 365,     prevalence_rendering_max_ages = 10 * 365,     human_population = human_pop   ) ) |>   malariasimulation::set_drugs(list(malariasimulation::SP_AQ_params)) |>   malariasimulation::set_smc(     drug = 1,     timesteps = smc_days,     coverages = smc_cov,     min_ages = rep(smc_min_age, length(smc_days)),     max_ages = rep(smc_max_age, length(smc_days))   ) |>   malariasimulation::set_bednets(     timesteps = itn_days,     coverages = itn_cov,     retention = retention,     dn0 = matrix(dn0, nrow = n_dist, ncol = 1),     rn = matrix(rn, nrow = n_dist, ncol = 1),     rnm = matrix(rnm, nrow = n_dist, ncol = 1),     gamman = gamman_vec   ) |>   malariasimulation::set_equilibrium(init_EIR = init_EIR)  ##Run malariasimulation malsim <- malariasimulation::run_simulation_with_repetitions(   timesteps = n_days,   repetitions = num_sims,   parameters = malsim_params )

title: Customising Simulation Outputs
text: One benefits malariasimple comparisons groups individuals can made easily using get_custom_output(). method requires extra step post-processing running simulation, however permits much flexibility regarding customising output. human variable can output, includes: Total humans "n" Clinical incidence "clin_inc" Detected cases "detect" Susceptibles "S" Diseased, untreaded "D" Asymptomatic infection "" Sub-patent infection "U" Treated Disease "T" Uninfected, prophylactically protected "P" can define subsection human population want outputs . can defined according three axes: Age Intervention category Biting group Using method two step process: Run simulation, specifying full_output = TRUE. Use get_custom_output() summarise desired output variables. example comparing malaria prevalence children received SMC .
code: library(malariasimple)  ## Set up parameters and run simulation #Define seasonality parameters g0 <- 41.27 g <- c(-57.96, 14.57, 7.23) h <- c(-35.22, 35.87, -14.93)  #Define SMC parameters smc_days <- c(545, 575, 605, 910, 940, 970) smc_cov <- 0.6  #Define a custom age vector age_vector <- c(0, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70) * 365  #Define malariasimple parameters smc_params <- malariasimple::get_parameters(n_days = 1000,                              age_vector = age_vector) |>   malariasimple::set_seasonality(g0,g,h) |>   malariasimple::set_smc(coverages = 0.6,           days = smc_days,           min_age = 1 * 365,           max_age = 5*365,           distribution_type = "correlated") |>   malariasimple::set_equilibrium(init_EIR = 30)  #Run simulation with 'full_output = TRUE' smc_sim <- malariasimple::run_simulation(smc_params, full_output = TRUE) |> as.data.frame()  ## Get customised outputs #Define ages of interest (in this case, all age categories within the SMC age boundaries) #Age categories are selected by their lower bound. Given the age_vector above #(...1, 2, 3, 5...), selecting lower bounds 1, 2 and 3 covers the bands [1,2), #[2,3) and [3,5) - i.e. ages 1 to 5 - which matches the SMC age range #(min_age = 1 year, max_age = 5 years) and the reported PfPR1-5. smc_ages <- c(1, 2, 3) * 365  #Get output for children who have received SMC smc_kids <- get_custom_output(   smc_params,   smc_sim,   output_variables = c("n", "detect"),   ages = smc_ages,   int_group = 3 )  #Get output for children who did not receive SMC non_smc_kids <- get_custom_output(   smc_params,   smc_sim,   output_variables = c("n", "detect"),   ages = smc_ages,   int_group = 1 )  ## Plot the results plot(   smc_kids$time, smc_kids$detect / smc_kids$n,   type = "l", col = "blue", lwd = 2,   xlab = "Time", ylab = expression(italic(Pf)*PR[1-5]),   ylim = c(0,1),   bty = "l" ) abline(v = smc_days, col = "darkgrey", lty = 2) lines(   non_smc_kids$time, non_smc_kids$detect / non_smc_kids$n,   col = "red", lwd = 2 ) legend(   "topright",   legend = c("SMC Recipients", "Non-SMC Recipients"),   col = c("blue", "red"), lty = 1, lwd = 2,   bty = "c", bg = "white" )

title: Set SMC parameters — set_smc
text: params malariasimple parameters drug Specify default drug parameters. See ?set_drug_params details coverages Numeric vector detailing proportion target age population receiving SMC distribution event. single value also accepted days Numeric vector detailing days SMC administered min_age Minimum age eligible SMC max_age Maximum age eligible SMC smc_clearance_lag . days receipt SMC infectious clearance drug_efficacy Proportion infections successfully cleared drug_rel_c Relative infectivity treated individuals infection clearing period. 1 indicates difference. 0 indicates forward infection. shape_smc Shape Weibull distribution describing prophylactic waning scale_smc Scale Weibull distribution describing prophylactic waning distribution_type SMC distributions can either delivered randomly across eligible population time "random", given children time "correlated".

title: malariasimple 0.1.0
text: Added stochastic version model, selectable via get_parameters(stochastic = TRUE). Added ability propagate parameter uncertainty drawing joint posterior distribution via parameter_draws argument get_parameters() (defaults "median", reproduces previous central estimates). See new parameter_draws_df dataset. Added fully correlated option ITN distribution via set_bednets(distribution_type = "correlated") (default remains "random"). Added seasonal malaria chemoprevention (SMC) via set_smc(). Added support time-varying extrinsic incubation period (eip). Added custom output post-processing helpers (get_custom_output(), make_2d()). run_simulation() now errors clearly set_equilibrium() called.

title: malariasimple 0.1.0
text: Corrected ITN insecticide decay rate use mean retention time (rate 1 / gamman), matching malariasimulation’s bednet_decay(). Fixed double-counting error ITN decay single distribution event specified.

title: malariasimple 0.1.0
text: changes alter model behaviour /public interface. Existing scripts need updating, numerical results may differ previous versions. het_brackets -> biting_groups ft -> daily_ft delayMos -> eip mu0 -> mum tau1 / tau2 -> foraging_time / gonotrophic_cycle bites_Bed / bites_Indoors -> phi_bednets / phi_indoors default parameter values changed: tsd (4 -> 3), number biting heterogeneity groups (5 -> 4), phi_bednets (0.89 -> 0.85), phi_indoors (0.97 -> 0.9). new human_pop argument (default 100000) now scales initial human state sizes. set_seasonality() now takes Fourier coefficients g0, g h directly instead season_params object. get_seasonal_forcing() get_peak_cc() signatures changed accordingly.
